events.label: Bessent 'Operation Economic Fury' press conference — Iran economic isolation plan details
events.note: Added Aug 21 night: Brent closed at $94.39 on Friday, crossing the formal $94 regime trigger, after Trump declared 'economic D-Day' against Iran and threatened secondary sanctions on any nation trading with Tehran. Bessent confirmed he will detail 'Operation Economic Fury' at a Monday press conference. Iranian President Pezeshkian issued the first substantive de-escalation language since the conflict began ('it is better to end the war today'), but no formal negotiating channel has opened. The press conference resolves the immediate direction: comprehensive secondary sanctions with no diplomatic off-ramp extends Brent above $96 and pressures 30Y toward 5.30%; diplomatic framing alongside Pezeshkian's signal could return Brent below $93 and deactivate the regime trigger before NVDA's Aug 26 print.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — Brent regime trigger now active entering print
events.note: Updated Aug 21 night: Brent closed at $94.39 — formal $94 regime trigger crossed. 30Y at 5.25%, 5bps from 5.30% bear trigger. AMD recovered to $473.25 (seven sessions below $484 containment, up from $466.71 Thursday — first recovery move). Flash composite PMI 56.0 (services 56.8 vs 54.0 estimate, 4-year high) supports enterprise AI demand; manufacturing miss and supply-chain stress at 13-month low are the cost headwind. ROST gap-and-fade below $235 closed the retail earnings gauntlet 3-1 (HD, TGT, ROST beat; WMT missed). Bar unchanged: gross margin above 78% AND data-center guide materially above ~$38–39B for Q3 FY28 revenue — both simultaneously required. Jackson Hole begins Aug 27 — no de-risk window between the print and Warsh's keynote. S&P −1.4% weekly, Nasdaq −2.0%; back-to-back weekly losses setting the macro backdrop.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote Aug 28; Brent regime trigger now active
events.note: Updated Aug 21 night: Brent crossed $94.39 (formal regime trigger breached). 30Y at 5.25%, 5bps from 5.30% trigger. Flash composite PMI 56.0 (services 56.8, 4-year high; manufacturing 53.2 miss, supply-chain stress at 13-month high). September hike odds 31% — bifurcated PMI and oil breach make the September 16 FOMC path highly uncertain. Warsh's Fri Aug 28 keynote (first as Fed Chair) is the session's defining event: does he frame Brent above $90 as a transitory geopolitical disruption (hold sufficient) or a sustained supply constraint (higher-for-longer risk)? With oil formally above the $94 threshold, the framing carries direct implications for long-duration assets. NVDA prints Aug 26 AH — one day before the symposium opens, no de-risk gap. UMich final (Aug 28) is a within-symposium data point; prior: 51.0 (multi-year low).

events.label: AVGO Q3 FY2026 earnings (est.) — through $380 structural support; VMware + AI concentration dual overhang
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: AVGO fell 5% to ~$362 on August 19, breaking through $380 structural support. VMware CVE-2026-59310 active exploitation (361 IPs, 47 countries per Aug 14 disclosure) + 72% AI revenue concentration (~72% of next-quarter sequential growth) create dual overhang. At ~65x trailing P/E, any miss or margin compression compounds. Q3 FY2026 results (est. September 4–5) are the first public accounting of both: VMware remediation costs in financial guidance, enterprise customer commentary on the incident, and AI revenue breadth. $380 is now resistance; $340–350 is the next structured support zone. Flip: recovery above $380 on volume, or formal VMware incident-containment statement before earnings.

events.label: Bessent Treasury long-dated buyback ops begin — $4B+ per op, 10-20yr and 20-30yr bonds
events.note: Added Aug 19 night: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced August 19 the department will double the size of long-dated bond buyback operations, raising the maximum per-operation from $2B to at least $4B for bonds maturing in the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year ranges. Effective September 9, runs through November 4 (end of current refunding quarter). Immediate market impact: 30Y fell 9bps to 5.196% on the announcement. The program provides structural demand support for the long end through the NVDA print (Aug 26), Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29), and into October. If underlying supply dynamics ($432B July deficit, $1.7T corporate issuance) overwhelm the $4B+ buyback, the 30Y could reassert above 5.25% before the program begins.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
